claims.text: Vibrating Sample Magnetometry can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
Ferromagnetic Resonance can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
Neutron diffraction can determine the presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs.
The relevant initial material is a near-equiatomic HEA.
Composition, processing method, and test conditions are varied as interventions.
Room-temperature magnetic characterization is applicable to the HEA.
Neutron diffraction is among the relevant test conditions.
Crystal structure and phase composition mediate the magnetic behavior.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties of HEAs is attributable to configurational entropy.
The correlation between electrical and magnetic properties of HEAs is attributable to the average ionic radius of an A-site cation.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius control the intensity of indirect super-exchange interactions.
Configurational entropy and A-site ionic radius promote the formation of ferromagnetic nanoclusters.
The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs can be tuned by varying composition.
The presence of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs can be tuned by varying processing method and test conditions.
Observation of saturation magnetization and remanent magnetization establishes a baseline for the presence of a ferromagnetic ground state.
The relevant boundary is a transition from a paramagnetic state to a ferromagnetic state.
Composition, processing method, and test conditions can shift the paramagnetic-to-ferromagnetic transition.
The exact mechanism of ferromagnetic ground states in HEAs remains uncertain and requires further experimental and theoretical investigation.
A systematic study using VSM, FMR, and neutron diffraction can test the proposed magnetic behavior.
Failure to observe ferromagnetic ground states under the tested variations would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial system is described as an alloy, whereas the mechanism invokes an A-site cation, terminology associated with site-defined oxide structures such as the cited perovskite high-entropy oxide. No A-site-bearing HEA is specified.
